notice: Examples only. Review each change against the application's requirements before applying; ACULYX never edits server files.

HSTS-001.note: Add includeSubDomains only when every subdomain supports HTTPS.

HSTS-002.summary: Raise HSTS max-age to at least one year.
HSTS-002.note: Add includeSubDomains only when every subdomain supports HTTPS.

HSTS-003.note: Verify HTTPS is available on all subdomains before enabling includeSubDomains.

HSTS-004.summary: Meet basic HSTS preload header prerequisites if preload is intended.
HSTS-004.note: This does not establish preload-list eligibility or membership. Verify all hstspreload.org requirements before submission.

HSTS-005.summary: Review HSTS preload if broad HTTPS enforcement is appropriate.
HSTS-005.note: ACULYX checks basic response directives only and does not check the public preload list.

CSP-001.summary: Start with a restrictive Content Security Policy.
CSP-001.note: A production policy must explicitly allow the application's required scripts, styles, images, and connections.

CSP-002.summary: Replace unsafe inline script permission with nonces or hashes.
CSP-002.note: Generate a cryptographically random nonce for each response and attach it to approved script elements.

CSP-003.summary: Remove unsafe-eval and refactor dynamic code evaluation.
CSP-003.note: Merge this directive into the existing policy; do not replace other required directives blindly.

CSP-004.summary: Replace wildcard script sources with an explicit host allowlist.
CSP-004.note: Use only origins that the application actually requires.

CSP-005.summary: Restrict which origins can frame this page.
CSP-005.note: This directive must be delivered as an HTTP response header; meta CSP cannot enforce it.

CSP-006.summary: Disable plugin object loading unless it is required.

CSP-007.summary: Restrict base URL changes from injected markup.

CSP-008.summary: Send CSP as a response header and review the meta policy separately.
CSP-008.note: The detected meta policy contents are not evaluated by ACULYX.

CSP-009.summary: Review bypass-prone script hosts and remove any that are not required.
CSP-009.note: The domain match is only a heuristic; inspect the specific endpoint, path, and library version before changing policy.

CSP-010.summary: Add a default-src or explicit script-src fallback to the CSP.
CSP-010.note: A policy without default-src or script-src provides no baseline script restriction.

CSP-REPORT-001.summary: Configure a CSP report-to group if violation telemetry is desired.
CSP-REPORT-001.snippet:
Reporting-Endpoints: csp="https://reports.example.com/csp"
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; report-to csp
CSP-REPORT-001.note: Use a privacy-reviewed endpoint and retain report-uri only as a compatibility fallback where needed.

COEP-001.summary: Enable cross-origin isolation only if the app requires it.
COEP-001.note: Audit all cross-origin resources before rollout; this can break embeds and third-party assets.

COEP-002.summary: Use a supported COEP value if cross-origin isolation is required.
COEP-002.note: credentialless is another supported mode where its cookie behavior is appropriate.

CORP-001.summary: Restrict cross-origin embedding when the resource is not intended to be shared.
CORP-001.note: Select same-site or cross-origin if required by how this resource is embedded.

CORP-002.note: Supported values are same-origin, same-site, and cross-origin.

CORP-003.summary: Review whether cross-origin embedding is intended.
CORP-003.note: Use same-site or cross-origin only when the resource sharing model requires it.

CORS-001.summary: Replace the CORS wildcard with an explicit origin allowlist.
CORS-001.note: Validate the request Origin header server-side against a fixed allowlist; do not reflect arbitrary origins.

PERMPOLICY-001.summary: Restrict sensitive browser features to explicit origins.

REPORT-001.summary: Configure browser reporting endpoints if reports are operationally useful.
REPORT-001.note: Reporting is optional; choose an endpoint and retention policy consistent with user privacy.

REPORT-002.summary: Align NEL report_to with a declared Reporting-Endpoints group.

REPORT-003.summary: Provide a valid NEL JSON object.

XFO-001.note: Use SAMEORIGIN if same-origin framing is required; CSP frame-ancestors is the modern control.

REF-001.summary: Limit referrer data sent to other origins.

DEP-001.note: Use a properly configured Content-Security-Policy instead.

DEP-002.note: Use certificate transparency monitoring and managed certificate lifecycle controls instead.

DEP-003.note: Modern browser privacy controls do not use P3P.

DEP-005.summary: Remove X-UA-Compatible if legacy IE document modes are not supported.

DEP-006.note: Modern browser certificate transparency policy is built in.

DEP-007.summary: Replace X-Content-Security-Policy with the standardized header.
DEP-007.note: Test the policy against application resources before enforcing.

DEP-008.summary: Replace X-WebKit-CSP with the standardized header.
DEP-008.note: Test the policy against application resources before enforcing.

DEP-009.note: HPKP is deprecated; use certificate transparency monitoring instead.

DEP-010.summary: Replace X-Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only with the standardized header.
DEP-010.note: Test the policy against application resources before promoting to enforcement.

DEP-011.summary: Replace X-WebKit-CSP-Report-Only with the standardized header.
DEP-011.note: Test the policy against application resources before promoting to enforcement.

DEP-012.note: This header is a legacy IE-specific directive and has no effect in modern browsers.

DOC-001.summary: Consider a Document-Policy for features the application does not need.
DOC-001.note: Document-Policy support and directives vary; choose only directives implemented by target browsers.

DUP-001.summary: Remove duplicate response headers and send each security header exactly once.
DUP-001.snippet: # Remove the duplicate header at your web server or reverse proxy configuration
DUP-001.note: Duplicate headers can cause browsers to apply only the first or last value, depending on the header; the effective policy may differ from what was intended.

INTEGRITY-001.summary: Consider Integrity-Policy for enforcing integrity metadata on scripts.
INTEGRITY-001.note: Inventory scripts and browser support before enforcing; this policy can block resources without integrity metadata.

LEAK-001.summary: Disable server version disclosure where supported.
LEAK-001.note: Framework and proxy settings vary; verify the final response headers.

CACHE-001.summary: Prevent shared caching of sensitive cookie-setting responses.
CACHE-001.note: Confirm this matches the endpoint's caching requirements.

COOK-001.note: Preserve the application's existing cookie value and scope.

COOK-003.summary: Add Secure when SameSite=None is required.
COOK-003.note: Use a stricter SameSite value if cross-site cookie use is unnecessary.

COOK-004.note: Use Strict or None only when the application's cross-site flow requires it.

COOK-005.summary: Use the __Host- prefix for eligible session cookies.
COOK-005.note: A __Host- cookie must omit Domain and use Path=/.

COOK-006.note: The cookie must be set over HTTPS.

COOK-007.summary: Fix the cookie attributes to match what its name prefix requires.
COOK-007.snippet:
Set-Cookie: __Host-session=<value>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly
Set-Cookie: __Secure-session=<value>; Secure
COOK-007.note: __Host- requires Secure, HttpOnly, Path=/, and no Domain attribute. __Secure- requires Secure. Browser will reject the cookie if requirements are not met.

SRI-001.summary: Add Subresource Integrity attributes to external scripts.
SRI-001.note: Generate integrity hashes with 'openssl dgst -sha384 -binary lib.js | openssl base64 -A'. Self-hosted scripts do not need SRI.

SUB-001.summary: Limit sensitive cookies to the host that needs them.
SUB-001.note: Omit Domain to create a host-only cookie.

SUB-002.summary: Remove broad subdomain trust from script-src.
SUB-002.note: Replace wildcard subdomain sources with specific trusted origins or nonces.

SUB-003.summary: Use an explicit CORS origin allowlist.
SUB-003.note: Validate the request Origin against a server-side allowlist; do not reflect arbitrary origins.

SUB-003H.summary: Ensure dynamic CORS reflection is intentional and secure.
SUB-003H.note: Vary: Origin indicates the server might reflect origins dynamically. Ensure it relies on an explicit allowlist, not arbitrary reflection.

SUB-004.summary: Restrict embedding to the same origin.
SUB-004.note: Deliver as an HTTP response header.

SUB-005.summary: Prefix sensitive cookies with __Host- where compatible.
SUB-005.note: Omit Domain; the prefix prevents subdomains from setting a competing cookie.

SUB-006.note: Test popup, OAuth, and cross-origin window workflows before rollout.

SUB-007.note: Check compatibility with any intentional document.domain usage.

SUB-008.summary: No change indicated by this informational finding.
SUB-008.note: The analyzed subdomain has no detected trust bridge to its registrable domain.

REDIR-001.summary: Review security headers across each redirect destination.
REDIR-001.snippet: # Configure required headers on the final destination response
REDIR-001.note: A redirecting response's policies do not automatically apply to the destination response.

CSP-002S.note: Allows injection of malicious CSS which can exfiltrate data via attribute selectors or deface the site.

CSP-SYNTAX-001.summary: Fix CSP syntax or nonce issues.

CSP-META-001.summary: Move CSP from a <meta> tag to a Content-Security-Policy HTTP response header.
CSP-META-001.recommendation: Move the CSP policy from a <meta> tag to a Content-Security-Policy HTTP response header. The HTTP header provides broader enforcement (navigation, workers, plugins) and should be the primary delivery mechanism. Keep the meta tag as a supplementary signal only.
